title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Busy travel weekend: a record-long FAA ground stop on Friday left lots of flyers stuck, though systems are back up and airlines expect most schedules to be on track by Sunday night. Microsoft's big outage is also officially fixed, Wu-Tang Clan's Rock Hall night went ahead as planned, and a couple in England is making street signs sparkle one scrub at a time. Around Charlotte, bundle up, because chilly mornings are here before a warm-up late next week.

stories.headline: Concord family safe after overnight house fire
stories.summary: A two-story home on Millstone Circle SW in Concord caught fire just after midnight Saturday. Crews from Concord and Harrisburg had it under control in under an hour, and no one was hurt. The Red Cross is helping the family, who had to leave the home.
key_facts: Firefighters were dispatched at 12:21 a.m. and arrived within 5 minutes
36 firefighters responded after a second alarm at 12:32 a.m.
Fire under control at 1:16 a.m.; no injuries reported
The Concord Fire Marshal's Office is investigating the cause
stories.why: Everyone got out safely, and a quick, well-coordinated response from several local agencies kept it from getting worse.

stories.headline: Flights still catching up after Friday's nationwide ground stop
stories.summary: A more than four-hour nationwide ground stop on Friday, the longest in 25 years, is still rippling through air travel. Officials blame an equipment outage linked to upgrading old technology, and the FAA says it doesn't believe it was a cyberattack. Charlotte Douglas saw more than 700 combined delays and cancellations on Saturday, with long rebooking lines.
key_facts: The FAA expected about 5,000 cancellations nationwide Saturday
About 1.5 million flyers had travel plans disrupted
Charlotte had 351 cancellations and 405 delays Saturday, per FlightAware
Most operations are expected to be back on track by Sunday night
stories.why: If you're flying soon, check your flight status before heading out. Things should be close to normal by Sunday night.

stories.headline: Microsoft's global outage is officially over
stories.summary: Microsoft says it has fully restored service after Thursday's outage knocked Outlook, Teams and Copilot offline in at least 74 countries and territories. The company said a technical issue caused it, not a cyberattack or AI. It is now warning about fake emails trying to take advantage of the outage.
key_facts: Microsoft blamed "elevated load" on its infrastructure
Fake emails imitating Microsoft notices say blocked messages will be deleted unless you click to restore them
Microsoft says these emails are part of an active phishing campaign
stories.why: Your email should be working again. Just don't click on any "restore your messages" emails.

links.title: Microsoft announces service ‘restored,’ global outage over

stories.headline: Charlotte: chilly mornings now, 70s by next weekend
stories.summary: Cold, clear nights are sticking around the Carolinas, with lows in the 20s and 30s and what WCNC calls the coldest night of the season so far. Days will be sunny and dry with highs in the 50s and 60s. A warming trend kicks in Thursday.
key_facts: Sunday: sunny and cold, highs in the 50s
Monday through Wednesday: sunny, highs in the 50s and 60s
Thursday and Friday: highs in the upper 60s to low 70s
Next weekend looks mild and dry, with highs in the 70s
stories.why: Grab a jacket for the mornings and enjoy plenty of sunshine, with a mild weekend ahead.

stories.headline: Jamaican singer Hope Vocals celebrates Maroon heritage in a new photo series
stories.summary: Singer Hope Vocals teamed up with American photographer Charles "Tingz" Ward on "Human Nature: Hope Vocals," a photo series shot in her home community of Moore Town, Portland. Ward discovered her through her Kumina Medley video. One standout portrait shows her holding a Maroon abeng, a traditional horn.
key_facts: Ward hopes to show the work in New York, Miami and Paris
Hope says the abeng reminds her that she is strong
Her video for "God's Timing" premiered October 23
stories.why: It's a lovely example of art helping a living culture reach new audiences.

links.title: Hope Vocals teams up with American photographer on new project

stories.headline: Drake's Stake lawsuit stays mostly on pause
stories.summary: A federal judge in New Mexico kept most of a gambling-promotion lawsuit against Drake, streamer Adin Ross and Stake.us on hold. The judge left one thing moving: Drake and Ross's requests to have the case dismissed because, they argue, New Mexico courts don't have authority over them. Everyone is waiting on a related arbitration question in an Illinois case.
key_facts: Chief U.S. District Judge Kenneth J. Gonzales signed the order Friday, November 13
Plaintiffs Nathaniel Torres and Rory Michie allege deceptive promotion lured them into gambling
The next status report is due February 11, 2027, or within 14 days of a ruling in the Illinois case
disputed: The deceptive-promotion claims are allegations only and haven't been proven in court
Confirmed: the partial pause, and that the dismissal motions are still pending
stories.why: Expect no big rulings in this case for a while.

stories.headline: Wu-Tang's Rock Hall night goes ahead despite the flight chaos
stories.summary: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame organizers said everyone performing at Saturday's induction in Los Angeles had already arrived before Friday's ground stop. Wu-Tang Clan got in on its first nomination, and Ol' Dirty Bastard's son, Young Dirty Bastard, was set to perform with the group. Queen Latifah, MC Lyte and Rick Rubin are also being honored.
key_facts: The ceremony was held at the Peacock Theater
Luther Vandross and Phil Collins are also first-time-nominee inductees
Sade, Oasis and Iron Maiden had already said they would skip, for reasons unrelated to the flights
The ceremony airs on ABC and Disney+ in December
stories.why: It's a big night for hip-hop history, and fans can catch it on TV in December.

stories.headline: Medical journals ask doctors to speak up on nuclear risk
stories.summary: Editors of more than 100 international journals published a joint editorial. It urges health professionals to keep health at the center of public discussions about nuclear risk, given rising geopolitical tensions.
key_facts: More than 100 journals took part in the joint editorial
stories.why: The medical community is asking that health be part of these big policy conversations.
